primary_findings: The explicit local component D-law fixed the Probe 016 safe over-blocking case for CREATE ui.toast@v3.
All specimens preserved split version token/ref shape and kept canonical_semantic_pointer null unless all components were admitted.
One gpt-5.4-mini specimen repaired the unknown operator FLORP into canonical_operator = CREATE while keeping the full pointer null.
One gpt-5.4-mini specimen had correct component values but used an overly broad canonical_lookup_status.
gpt-5.4 passed all four component-admission cases exactly.
evidence_boundary: Probe 017 supports the split version token/ref schema and local component-admission D-law.
Probe 017 does not prove low-end residents can reliably author canonical component fields without harness validation.
Probe 017 strengthens the case that routing statuses should be harness-computed or heavily closed/remanded.
recommended_next_iteration: Move canonical component admission and routing statuses toward harness-computed fields.
If continuing prompt-level tests, run a focused remand probe for FLORP ui.menu@v1 where canonical_operator was incorrectly repaired to CREATE.
Keep testing full pointer safety separately from local component precision.
overall_assessment: Probe 017 is a strong confirmation of the split version/ref and local component-admission design, with a remaining low-end nearest-operator repair leak at the canonical component level and a separate routing-status precision miss.
